subject: DPA clarifications: controller/processor, subprocessors, breach notice
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@summitbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@summitbank.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up on DPA items from earlier today

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning - helpful overview. As we dig into procurement with our legal/compliance team, a few items came up that we need clarified in the DPA/addendum before we can move forward: 

- Controller vs. processor: we need explicit language confirming Summit Bank is the controller and Redwood is the processor for customer data processed via the hosted API.
- Subprocessors: can you provide a current list of subprocessors (and a cadence for notification when new subprocessors are added)?
- Breach notice: what is Redwood's contractual maximum notification timeline once a confirmed data breach affecting Summit Bank data has been identified?
- Data residency & PII: our customers require EU residency for EU-origin PII. Can you confirm region-level data residency options and controls?
- Logging/retention: what logs are retained (request/response metadata, full payloads) and for how long? Is there a way to limit retention for PII on a per-account basis?

Can you loop in whoever handles legal/infosec so we can get a formal response and an updated redline? We can target a follow-up call early next week if that helps.

Appreciate it,
Alex

--

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@summitbank.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@summitbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on DPA items from earlier today

Hi Alex / Priya -

Thanks for outlining these items. Quick answers below; happy to discuss live if helpful.

1) Controller / Processor- Contractually we accept PSAs where the customer is the controller and Redwood is the processor for customer-provided data. We use standard processor obligations (security measures, subprocessors, instructions, deletion on termination). If you have specific controller obligations you want reflected, send redlines and we can review.

2) Subprocessors- Current list (attached): subprocessors_list.csv. We publish an up-to-date list here: https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors.
- Notification cadence: we notify customers 30 days in advance for new subprocessors that will have access to production data; we will offer an opt-out if a subprocessor materially changes processing scope (per standard carve-outs).

3) Breach notice- Our contractual standard is to notify customers "without undue delay" and provide updates as we investigate. For high-severity incidents affecting customer data, we commit to an initial notification within 72 hours of confirming the breach and have a post-incident report within 30 days where feasible.

4) Data residency & EU PII- Hosted: we support region-specific routing and storage for customers on dedicated plans (Dedicated or Private) and can offer EU-only residency for EU-origin PII. For shared-hosted instances we can support EU region deployment for your data; we can add specific residency language in the addendum and SOW.

5) Logging & retention- We retain request/response metadata (timestamps, request size, model, latency) for 13 months by default for billing/operational purposes. Full request/response payloads (including prompts/responses) are retained for 30 days by default and can be configured with shorter retention on Dedicated/Private plans.
- For PII: we offer a data deletion endpoint and contractual deletion on termination. We can also provide a per-account opt-in for no-payload retention (metadata-only) or on-demand redaction for specific records - these are commonly handled via an SOW or configuration on Dedicated/Private contracts.

Attachments: subprocessors_list.csv

Let me know if you'd like specific contract language and I'll propose redlines for the DPA.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@summitbank.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@summitbank.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on DPA items from earlier today

Dev / Marissa -

Appreciate the quick answers. A few follow-ups from our security/compliance reviewers:

- Can you provide the exact contractual clause text you propose for the controller/processor sentence so our counsel can review?
- On subprocessors: the published list is fine; would Redwood accept a clause requiring 30-days notice and an explicit right for Summit to object and request an alternative (e.g., host in dedicated region) for subprocessors who process EU-origin PII?
- Breach notice: 72 hours for confirmed high-severity incidents is acceptable. Can you confirm this will be written as an explicit contractual obligation (not just "without undue delay")?
- Retention: the 30-day full payload retention is short, thanks. For our use case we need a contractual option to have full payloads deleted within 7 days for EU-origin PII and 90 days for US-origin PII; can we get that as part of our addendum?
- Data deletion on termination: can you add a clause committing to cryptographic deletion of keys (where applicable) and confirmation within 30 days of termination?

If you can send a redline with the proposed DPA language addressing the bullet points above, we can get our legal team to review ahead of Monday's call.

Best,
Alex
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@summitbank.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@summitbank.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on DPA items from earlier today

Alex / Priya -

Thanks - that's really helpful context. We're drafting an annotated redline now and attaching an updated DPA excerpt that incorporates:

- Explicit controller/processor sentence calling out Summit Bank as controller and Redwood as processor, with a short clause on processing strictly on documented instructions.
- Subprocessor clause with 30-day notice and explicit right to object; operational workaround language for dedicated hosting where feasible.
- Breach clause with a 72-hour initial notification commitment for confirmed high-severity incidents and a timeline for post-incident reporting.
- Retention options: we'll add contract language to allow 7-day EU full-payload deletion and 90-day US full-payload deletion as an addendum option for Summit Bank on hosted vs. dedicated plans.
- Deletion on termination: we'll incorporate a clause for cryptographic key destruction (where applicable) and confirmation within 30 days.

Attachments: DPA_redline_SummitBank_20260803.pdf

Next steps:
1) Dev will post the proposed redline to this thread by end of day so you can circulate to your counsel.
2) If the Monday 2026-08-03 10:00 PT call still works, let's keep that - otherwise propose an alternative.

Happy to adjust language where needed - thanks again for the clear asks.

Best,
Marissa
